Italy’s new cover star enjoyed a ‘beautiful’ treble but could not celebrate it after his side threw away two-goal leads three times to draw 4-4 with Atalanta
T his ought to have been a magic moment for Pio Esposito. He had just scored his first Serie A hat-trick, becoming only the third Italian to get one for Inter in the era of three points for a win. The last to do it was Christian Vieri, back in 2003. Two years before Esposito was born.
We will come back to that. Esposito has been drawing premature comparisons to Vieri for some time and especially now after a barnstorming November in which he has scored eight times in five games, including three in two for his country, and two of those as part of a man-of-the-match performance during an upset win against France .
He was the nation’s cover star after that win, variously punching the air, roaring or spreading arms open wide across the front pages of Italy’s sports newspapers. His body language on Sunday night was different. By the end of Inter’s 4-4 draw with Atalanta , Esposito carried the haunted look of a Dickensian protagonist who had just been visited by the ghost of Belgium past.
“I’m really struggling to give an explanation right now,” Esposito told the TV cameras when asked how his team had failed to win a game that they led 2-0, 3-1 and finally 4-2 as late as the 76th minute. “It’s a beautiful thing [to score the hat-trick] but I’m having a hard time enjoying it because we threw two points away.”
A sentiment that can only have been heightened by a sense of history repeating. Esposito’s goals against France had put Italy on course for the quarter-finals of the Nations League. All they needed to do was draw their final group game away to Belgium. Esposito struck again to give them an early lead at the King Baudouin Stadium. And then they collapsed to a 4-1 defeat.
These stories share another recurring character: Charles De Ketelaere. He provided the assists on Belgium’s first and third goals, turning that game on its head in the space of 10 minutes. On Sunday, he was at it again, scoring Atalanta’s second and third goals then winning the penalty from which his teammate Franck Kessié finally equalised in second-half stoppage time.
Even by the standards of this barmy Serie A season, on a weekend that gave us two 5-1 scorelines and a 4-0, this was a preposterous game of football. Inter looked completely in control heading into the final 20 minutes, leading 3-1 thanks to Esposito’s hat-trick.
He might have made it to three before half-time if Marco Sportiello had not denied him from point-blank range when the score was still 1-0. Instead, Esposito had to wait until just after the interval to bag his third, running on to a Marcus Thuram through ball and lifting it over the Atalanta keeper.
None of the three goals were spectacular, but together they illustrated what a menace Esposito has become. For the first, he simply held his spot in the middle of the penalty area after an initial cross was half-cleared, punishing Atalanta’s defence for losing its shape on the second ball. His second was a glancing header at a corner.
In moments like this, it is easy to see why people want to make that link to Vieri, another powerful Inter No 9 who could dominate in the air. But, leaving aside the obvious point that we are comparing a 21-year-old with 13 top-flight goals to a player who won both Serie A’s capocannoniere award and the Pichichi trophy for top scorer in La Liga, is that even the most apt former star to draw parallels with?
Vieri has said that anyone who thinks they are similar “doesn’t understand much about football”, noting that Esposito’s 6ft 3in height and broad-shouldered physique remind him more of Luca Toni.
Esposito’s brothers Salvatore and Sebastiano – both also professional footballers – have compared him to another former Inter player, Edin Dzeko, whom he looked up to while working his way through the club’s academy. There are certainly echoes of the Bosnian in the work he does as an attacking pivot, holding off defenders to make space for runners from midfield.
But Esposito will not be a carbon copy of any player who has gone before him. Part of the thrill of seeing him excel for club and country over the last month has been watching him start to define himself as confidence grows. He played 48 times for Inter last season, yet always was the understudy to Thuram and Lautaro Martínez. This campaign already feels different. He is becoming a main character in his own right.
If only his supporting casts could perform to the same level. Eljif Elmas’s first goal back for Atalanta had been fortuitous, the ball coming back to him after a first scuffed shot was blocked by Federico Dimarco. After Esposito’s third goal, there were 20 minutes in which Maurizio Sarri’s team barely fashioned a chance. Inter contrived to give them a way back in.
De Ketelaere’s first goal came out of the blue, a header from a corner. Was Esposito himself at fault for not being closer to the Belgian as he leapt in a failed attempt to intercept the cross? In any case, Inter responded immediately, Petar Sucic scoring from the penalty spot after Davide Zappacosta fell and handled the ball while trying to cut out a cross from Thuram.
That should have been the end of things, but it wasn’t. Atalanta’s English winger Jonathan Rowe was allowed to twinkle-toe along the byline and flick an outside-of-the-boot pass back to an entirely unmarked De Ketelaere, who smashed home from the middle of the box. Then, in the 90th minute, the Belgian headed the ball on to Alessandro Bastoni’s outstretched arm, earning the spot-kick that Kessié converted.
Had De Ketelaere also fouled Bastoni while challenging for the ball? Inter had a stronger claim that Zappacosta ought to have been shown a red card for his handball. It was the Zappacosta’s blocked cross that wound up falling to Rowe before Atalanta’s third goal.
But Inter’s manager, Cristian Chivu, is not one to indulge that sort of self-pity. His focus after the game was all on his own team’s mistakes, noting that none of the goals they conceded had come in transition but always “ a difesa schierata ” – with defenders in position who ought to have known better how to manage the threats they faced.
Como 2-0 Cagliari, Lazio 3-0 Lecce, Parma 1-5 AS Roma, Napoli 1-0 Torino Juventus 4-0 Venezia, Bologna 1-1 Udinese, Sassuolo 0-2 Genoa, Milan 5-1 Frosinone, Atalanta 4-4 Inter
“We will learn our lesson,” he insisted, but Inter fans will want to see words matched by deeds. Their team already shipped four goals once before this season, in a home Champions League defeat by Club Brugge. They have conceded 17 in 12 Serie A games.
The time had come to move no from a 38-year-old Francesco Acerbi and 34-year-old Stefan de Vrij this summer, but the current defence is performing far below the standards they previously helped to set. The sight of John Stones on the bench was encouraging after his hamstring troubles but Inter did concede three times in the one game he has started this season, against Udinese.
At least it will be a while before they, and Esposito, have to see De Ketelaere again. Sarri has been getting much better performances from the Belgian since adjusting Atalanta’s formation to make room for him as a No 10 but still hedged his praise at full-time, saying De Ketelaere still needs to perform with greater continuity: “Physically and technically, though, he’s one of the best I have ever coached.”

Futbol yolculuğuna henüz 9 yaşındayken adım atan Arda Güler , kısa sürede sahadaki oyun zekâsı ve sol ayağındaki sihirle yaşıtlarından sıyrılmayı başardı. Türkiye’den İspanya ’nın en görkemli kulübüne uzanan bu kariyer basamakları, tam anlamıyla bir azim ve yetenek hikâyesini gözler önüne seriyor. Genç yıldızın 13 yaşından 21 yaşına kadar geçirdiği o çarpıcı dönüşüm adım adım kayıtlara geçti.
İspanya La Liga devi Real Madrid, milli yıldızımız Arda Güler ’in geleceğine dair uzun süredir merakla beklenen resmi adımı attı. 2023 yılında Fenerbahçe ’den büyük umutlarla kadroya katılan genç yeteneğin 2029 yılında sona erecek mevcut kontratı, üç yıl daha uzatılarak 2032 yılına kadar garanti altına alındı. Henüz 21 yaşında olmasına rağmen Avrupa futbolunun zirvesinde adından sıkça söz ettiren Arda Güler’in bu dev imzası, kariyerindeki baş döndürücü yükselişi ve son 8 yılda yaşadığı inanılmaz değişimi yeniden gündeme taşıdı.
13 Yaş: Gençlerbirliği altyapısında parlayan yeteneğiyle dikkat çekti ve Fenerbahçe altyapısına transfer olarak kariyerinin ilk büyük kırılma anını yaşadı.
15 Yaş: Sarı-lacivertli kulüple ilk profesyonel sözleşmesine imza atarak A takım kapısını araladı.
16 Yaş: Fenerbahçe U19 takımına yükseldiği dönemde sergilediği performansla A takımda ilk resmi maçına çıktı.
17 Yaş: Fenerbahçe A takımı formasıyla fileleri havalandırarak ilk gol sevincini yaşadı ve tribünlerin sevgilisi haline geldi.
18 Yaş: Sarı-lacivertli forma altında Türkiye Kupası zaferi yaşadı. Hemen ardından 20 milyon euro bonservis bedeli ve bonuslar karşılığında dünya devi Real Madrid’e transfer oldu. Aynı yaş diliminde eflatun-beyazlı formayla ilk maçına çıkıp İspanya Süper Kupası’nı kaldırdı.
19 Yaş: Real Madrid kariyerinde kupa koleksiyonunu genişletti. La Liga, UEFA Şampiyonlar Ligi , UEFA Süper Kupası ve FIFA Kıtalararası Kupa şampiyonluklarına ulaşırken ligde 6 gol kaydetti.
21 Yaş: Real Madrid formasıyla 100. resmi maçına çıkarak 'dalya' dedi. 2025-2026 sezonunda UEFA Şampiyonlar Ligi’nin Çıkış Yapan Oyuncusu seçildi ve son olarak 2032 yılına kadar sürecek yeni sözleşmeye imza attı.

German giants’ treatment of midfielder has raised questions about how far the reputation of a family club still holds
I t was, on paper, a perfect Friday evening for Bayern to flex their muscles once again, in the chill of their intimidating Allianz Arena against struggling opponents who had won just twice all season in the league. In the end, though, the best news of the night was that Saïd El Mala, the star of the visitors, Köln, who had scored a jaw-dropping consolation goal at the same stadium in spring, fluffed a far easier chance in the closing stages that would have condemned the champions to defeat.
The word crisis is rampantly overused in sport, but this was the weekend Bayern’s injury troubles reached critical mass. With Luis Díaz, Serge Gnabry and Ismaël Saibari already missing, their talisman Harry Kane had his game curtailed after 20 minutes and by the time the second half had begun, they’d lost Michael Olise too.
Olise inspired perhaps the greatest trepidation, leaving the stadium on crutches, though it looked worse than it was. The Frenchman could even be available for the midweek trip to Lille in the Champions League, though, given the current shortages in the front part of the squad especially, it feels like he might be better off being kept at home with his valuable feet up. Losing Kane, however, will have to be coped with. He has already had an operation to fix torn ankle ligaments. The England captain is not expected back for three months. “We now have seven games [until the winter break] with the squad we have,” said Bayern’s sporting director, Max Eberl, acknowledging that the loss of Kane was “a huge blow for all of us”. He hinted that Bayern will be ready to compensate for those losses in the transfer window.
Yet remarkably none of these – the sporting slip-up nor the growing injury headaches – were the headline. Just as this should have been a procession for Bayern, this should have been a happy return for Jamal Musiala, back as a substitute after more than two months out. Yet a cloud had hung over the No 10 since a very public discussion was begun by – of course – Uli Hoeness about reviewing the player’s lucrative contract, running until 2030 at a reported €25m (£20.9m) annually, should his injury and illness issues prevent him returning to his best form.
Karl-Heinz Rummenigge added fuel to the fire at full-time by actually backing his longtime colleague Hoeness, calling the latter’s words “perfectly understandable”. Rummenigge continued, referring to Musiala’s neurological condition – managed with medication – which caused him to collapse in successive pre-season games in August. “You have to talk to the family, to the player, and especially to the agency, because these sums [Musiala’s wages] are – with all due respect – no longer justifiable.”
The mushrooming situation forced Fifpro to step in on Saturday afternoon, with the union stating they were “deeply concerned by the repeated public statements from FC Bayern’s leadership”. underlining the club’s duty to look after a player attempting to recover his best, rather than applying publicly pressure to him amid negotiations with Musiala’s representatives which have gone on since summer, according to Süddeutsche Zeitung. “Making Musiala’s health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure,” the statement continued. “Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.”
Hoeness and Rummenigge can be expected to speak their minds, two giants of the club’s history no longer in key decision-making positions but with names and voices still able to make waves in public. Arguably the real issue was the CEO, Jan-Christian Dreesen, who had fallen short in defusing the situation in midweek. He initially talked about not putting Musiala under pressure. “He needs time to come back. He has to get that time.” Yet Dreesen finished his comments by adding “and then we’ll see how things look at the beginning of next year,” again (unhelpfully) applying a time frame. For somebody at the head of a global giant to frame his point so clumsily is damaging.
This is the crux of the matter. Bayern’s public treatment of Musiala, as if he were somehow to blame for being injured (which has covered the bulk of his unavailability) and ill and continuing to get paid, is chipping away at their image as a superclub apart, more family-focused and in touch with their roots than their European peers. That has been felt among the fanbase which, in keeping with German supporter power, always makes clear any issues with the club’s hierarchy. One supporter, the neurologist Jonatan Hoffmann, took the stage at Saturday’s club AGM to chide the club for their handling of the situation, emphasising Musiala needed support to widespread applause.
Yet beyond the fans, there are more than ripples. Maik Franz, the vice-president of the German players’ union (VDV) called Bayern’s dealing with the situation “shabby and unprofessional” in a column for Kicker, while former Bayern stars including Lothar Matthäus and Steffen Effenberg were scathing of their old club in the media over the weekend. Effenberg told Sport 1’s Doppelpass on Sunday that the behaviour of the Bayern big wigs had been “catastrophic”.
All of this will be enormously frustrating for Vincent Kompany, the man who should have been the week’s story but ended up as a footnote. He was appearing on the touchline for the first time since his frightening collapse during an under-23s training session at the club’s Säbener Strasse headquarters. When Kompany appeared before the media for the first time since his hospitalisation on Thursday, he appeared with his left arm in a sling having landed on and dislocated his shoulder, which required surgery, when he fell.
Kompany thanked a packed press conference for their concern, and swiftly announced he was fine and there was nothing more to talk about. Typical Kompany; adroit, aware, and draining all the drama out of the situation. Much of the success in recent seasons has been built on the calm that Kompany has brought to Bayern. To come back after a few weeks off to find the artists formerly known as FC Hollywood again airing their dirty linen in public is the last thing he wanted, or needed. The smell may take a while to dissipate.
Bayern Munich 1-1 Cologne, Elversberg 0-1 Freiburg, Borussia M’gladbach 0-1 Borussia Dortmund, Bayer Leverkusen 4-0 Paderborn, Eintracht Frankfurt 1-0 Hoffenheim, Union Berlin 1-5 RB Leipzig, Schalke 0-0 Stuttgart, Augsburg 3-1 Mainz, Werder Bremen 4-0 Hamburg
Another should-have-been headliner from Friday night was Köln’s Mikey Moore, with the teenage Tottenham loanee opening the scoring in a 1-1 draw by artfully finishing off a flowing move for his debut Bundesliga goal.
Bayern faltering makes Borussia Dortmund leaders, but only just. It took a late Felix Nmecha winner – and a clanger from goalkeeper Daniel Batz – at Borussia Mönchengladbach to put them there, with the midfielder shelving his controversial crown celebration after a word from Jürgen Klopp on international duty. “That doesn’t mean I’ll never do that celebration again,” he said after the game, with CEO Carsten Cramer and Hans-Joachim Watzke clear at Sunday’s AGM to recognise both Nmecha’s right to express his beliefs and fans’ rights to critique “aspects of the celebration linked to organisations whose values do not fully align with those of BVB”.
After a cagey opening Werder Bremen took the 111th edition of Nordderby with Hamburg in the second half, inspired by Hamburg-born Justin Njinmah (who had to skip the post-match celebrations with his wife going into labour) and with Niclas Füllkrug’s late strike making him the first player to reach double figures in this season’s Bundesliga.

Chelsea have suffered back-to-back defeats in the Premier League and are slipping towards the middle of the table; the Blues have won just once in five games in all competitions; watch Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea live on Sky Sports this Friday, kick-off 8pm
In his latest Sky Sports column, Paul Merson has raised doubts about whether Xabi Alonso is good enough as Chelsea manager - after another disappointing defeat in the Premier League.
The Blues were beaten 4-1 by arch-rivals Leeds at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, with the Blues now on a run of just one win in their last five matches in all competitions.
Chelsea have now slipped down to eighth place - and sit five points behind the top four. They do sit two points behind fifth, but Brentford could go ahead of the Blues if they win on Monday Night Football against Everton.
Merson believes Liverpool may have snubbed Alonso for the head coach role - eventually taken by Andoni Iraola - due to concerns about his pedigree.
There was no vacancy at Liverpool by the time Alonso took the Chelsea role on May 17, with Liverpool not sacking Arne Slot until June 1.
My biggest worry is that Liverpool could have had Xabi Alonso and they chose not to. Obviously, Liverpool didn't think he was good enough.
Alonso took the Chelsea job and Liverpool sacked Arne Slot two weeks later. You can't tell me that Liverpool couldn't have spoken to Alonso and say: 'Don't take the Chelsea job, we're going to take you'.
He was out of a job as well, Liverpool could have had him and he'd have gone there all day long. So why didn't they take him? Did they know something that we're seeing now?
It just always sits in my mind. That was my worry - and now it's playing out.
If this was Liam Rosenior in charge at Chelsea and getting these results, he'd be in major trouble. One hundred percent, he'd be in trouble. And remember, Rosenior didn't have Morgan Rogers in his Chelsea team, bought for £116m.
But it's because of the unbelievable job he did at Bayer Leverkusen that everybody is thinking: it will be alright.
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Tottenham and Leeds at home are Chelsea's two biggest games of the season for the fans - and they've lost them both. But while they're big for the fans, I'm not sure the players think that way. Not at all.
They probably think their biggest games are Arsenal, Manchester United and Manchester City.
The Leeds game changed when Moises Caicedo came off. For all the money they've spent… take Caicedo and Joao Pedro out of that team and Chelsea aren't good enough. They're the two players you cannot afford to miss.
They're not dominating football matches. The other major problem is defending. The goals they give away, the way it happens - it's mind-blowing. It's poor defending. Inexperienced defending.
The first goal against Leeds, Josh Acheampong gets stuck under the ball. I know he's a young kid but he still can't make that mistake. Then the ball gets to Noah Okafor, and Levi Colwill just jockeys to the side of him. He has to do something to stop that shot happening. He just dangles his leg out.
It's not be-all-and-end-all defending. You look at players like Dan Burn and Lewis Dunk for Newcastle and Brighton. They would dive in front of the ball and let the ball be smashed against them.
Sol Campbell, Tony Adams, Rio Ferdinand and Nemanja Vidic all had that mentality. Their job was to make sure you didn't score - and if you did, you'd have to produce something special to beat them. I just don't see that with Chelsea's defenders. It all seems far too easy.
We're talking about two Chelsea centre-halves, who are meant to be top drawer. One of them is an England international, and a future England captain not long ago in Levi Colwill. And then Wesley Fofana cost Chelsea £70m at a time when £70m was a lot of money.
Maxence Lacroix hasn't pulled up trees at Chelsea either. When he went off injured, it wasn't as if everyone had their head in their hands like if Caicedo or Pedro went off like that.
I expected Chelsea to get in the Champions League this season. Get in that competition and it's a great season. They're a million miles off winning the league.
The problem is there are a lot of teams above them. But now I don't see them beating Nottingham Forest on Friday, after what Forest did to Manchester City a few weeks ago.
That's a huge, huge, huge game at the City Ground. Every game you play for Chelsea is big, but if they win it - then I'd expect them to beat Crystal Palace after all and it's all looking rosy again.
They need Joao Pedro back. We go on about their front three. But if you had The Three Musketeers but took one of them out, you'd struggle to sell a film.

Galatasaray 'ın milli futbolcusu Abdülkerim Bardakcı'nın memleketi ve aile kökeni futbolseverler tarafından merak ediliyor. Özellikle sosyal medyada gündeme gelen paylaşımların ardından "Abdülkerim Bardakcı nereli, Kürt mü?" soruları araştırılıyor. Detaylar haberimizde.
Türkiye Futbol Federasyonunun resmi futbolcu bilgi bankasında yer alan bilgilere göre Abdülkerim Bardakcı, Konya'nın Meram ilçesinde dünyaya geldi. 7 Eylül 1994 doğumlu olan futbolcunun doğum yeri TFF kayıtlarında Meram olarak belirtiliyor.
Abdülkerim Bardakcı'nın Kürt olup olmadığına ilişkin kamuoyuna yansımış doğrulanmış bir bilgi veya kendi tarafından yapılmış açık bir etnik köken açıklaması bulunmuyor. Bu nedenle futbolcunun etnik kimliği hakkında kesin bir değerlendirme yapmak mümkün değil.
Abdülkerim Bardakcı'nın doğum yeri resmi kayıtlarda Konya'nın Meram ilçesi olarak yer alıyor. Ancak doğum yeri bilgisi, tek başına bir kişinin aile kökenini veya etnik kimliğini ortaya koymuyor. Futbolcunun ailesinin kökenine ilişkin doğrulanmış ayrıntılar da kamuoyuyla paylaşılmış değil.
